title: trace-ops-standup-rotations-2026-03-12
content:
Date: 2026-03-12
Owner: Emma Liu
Context: weekly lightweight capture from trace-ops/standup rotation. Focus this week: sampling experiment, dashboard tidy, cost telemetry spike investigation from 03-09 incident, and small instrumentation backlog. This is intentionally informal — notes to self + handoff doc for next rotation.

Attendees / async updates:
- Emma: ran the sampling experiment night runs; collected 72h of traces across prod region A/B, saw initial cost signal.
- Diego: dashboard prune + migrated model-latency panel to new metrics schema; left TODOs for per-model breakdown.
- Priya: investigated redis eviction correlation with KV-cache miss cascades; confirmed via trace spans.
- Jonah: started instrumenting the batcher service to emit per-batch size histograms (proto change in PR 212).
- Kai: rolled a minor alert threshold change to reduce noise on cold-starts.

Quick summary / outcome:
- Sampling experiment (reduced sample rate from 1.0 -> 0.25 for low-cardinality internal routes) produced an estimated trace storage cost reduction of ~17–22% across sampled services. p95 tracing capture completeness for customer-facing routes maintained above 98% (target 95%).
- Root cause for 03-09 latency spike: cascade of KV-cache misses + Redis evictions during a burst of long-sequence requests for model v2.3. Eviction events aligned with 03:14–03:29 UTC; redis-maxmemory config on a subset of nodes caused early evictions.
- Dashboards: replaced three deprecated panels and consolidated model latency into a single per-route heatmap. Remaining gaps: embedder latency missing in the new schema (tracked in OBS-4190).

Detailed notes:
1) Sampling experiment (Emma + Priya)
   - Hypothesis: many internal low-cardinality routes (healthchecks, metrics-pings, telemetry-pings) consume disproportionate trace storage and dilute useful signal.
   - Approach: use dynamic sampler: route-level classifier -> static weight 0.25 for routes in allowlist 'internal-low-card' (health, metrics, probe), keep 1.0 for customer routes and model-generation traces.
   - Data collected: 72h window, regions A + B, ~1.1M traces pre-change, ~320k traces post-change on low-card routes.
   - Metrics: trace storage GB/day dropped 19% on average; ingestion write ops decreased similarly. Token-level cost showed negligible change (traces are small compared to token storage); main win is storage and indexing cost.
   - Risks/notes: kafka partition skew observed during first rollout (consumer backpressure) — mitigated by increasing trace-ingest parallelism from 8 -> 12.
   - Next steps: extend dynamic sampling to edge routers and run 7d A/B test. File: link to PR and experiment dashboard in linked_artifacts.

2) 03-09 cost/latency spike investigation (Priya)
   - Symptom: sustained p99/p999 latency spikes for route /v1/generate between 03:12–03:40 UTC; cost telemetry spiked contemporaneously.
   - Tracing evidence: repeated spans with 'kv_lookup' -> 'redis_get' that had 'redis:evicted' tag present in ~27% of traces during window. Cache hit ratio dropped from 92% -> 61%.
   - Root cause: subset of redis nodes had smaller memory limit (legacy config after node replacement). Under burst, eviction cycle invalidated large number of cache entries.
   - Mitigation deployed: revert node-to-node mismatch config and increased memory on affected nodes; warmed cache via synthetic replay job for popular keys.
   - Follow-ups: add a probe metric that reports eviction_rate / minute per redis node to dashboard; add an alert if eviction_rate > 5/min for > 5m. Tracked in JIRA OBS-4182.

3) Dashboards + grooming (Diego)
   - Work done: removed 6 low-use panels, consolidated per-model latency into heatmap + per-tier filter (hosted/dedicated/private).
   - Shortcomings: embedder/encoder latency not surfaced in new schema (mismatch between telemetry v1 and v2). Need a small shim to expose those histograms to Grafana.
   - UX note: added linkouts from model-latency card to the trace explorer filtered by trace tags (model_version, route).
   - Action: Diego to complete shim by EOD 2026-03-15 (OBS-4190).

4) Instrumentation backlog (Jonah + Kai)
   - Jonah PR 212: adds batch_size histogram and 'batch_size' attribute on model forward spans. Reason: enable batching cost analyses and to calibrate batching thresholds in Redwood Optimize.
   - Kai: added a minor runbook step to check 'batch_size' distribution after deploy.
   - TODOs: add auto-alert if batch_size median < 2 for > 10% of requests for 15m (indicates poor batching during traffic dips).

5) Alerts and runbooks (team)
   - Quiet runbook edits: adjusted the trace-sampling rollback steps to include 'increase ingest parallelism' as a mitigation for observed kafka backpressure.
   - Reduced noise: lowered severity for cold-start tail alerts that fire during deployments from P2 -> P3. Documented reasoning in runbook (link in linked_artifacts).

Action items (owner — due)
- Emma: extend sampling A/B test to edge routers (add config + dashboard) — due 2026-03-19.
- Priya: implement eviction_rate probe and alert (OBS-4182) — due 2026-03-16.
- Diego: deliver embedder shim and update model-latency card (OBS-4190) — due 2026-03-15.
- Jonah: merge PR 212 and coordinate canary deploy; validate batch_size histograms appear in traces — due 2026-03-14.
- Kai: update runbook with kafka mitigation steps and notify SREs — due 2026-03-13.

Open questions / discussion points:
- Sampling policy: what's minimum sample rate for internal routes before we lose actionable debugging signal? Tentatively 0.1 but want more evidence.
- Runbook complexity: should we embed a quick rollback playbook in the alert pages to avoid paging on basic sampling rollbacks?
- Cost visibility: how best to attribute trace storage cost back to product features (model ledger vs infra)? Need product finance input.

Notes to next rotation / handoff:
- If you see ingestion lag in the tracing pipeline after rolling sampling changes: first increase trace-ingest consumer parallelism, then temporarily revert sampler to 1.0 for the affected route, then open OBS-4182.
- CLI snippets I used: 
  - curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/v1/query?query=trace_storage_gb%5B1d%5D" | jq .
  - kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --describe --group trace-ingest | grep Lag
  - redis-cli -h redis-prod-12 info memory | grep used_memory_human

Misc / notes to self:
- Cross-compare indexing cost vs cold storage tier for trace archives; possible larger cost win if we move old traces to cheaper tier after 14 days.
- Look into whether span-level TTL (for low-value spans) could be applied at ingest to reduce index size.

Meeting cadence / next check-in:
- Quick async standup daily; full sync next Friday 2026-03-19 at 10:00 PT (agenda: sampling A/B decisions, eviction alert rollouts, dashboard SHIP).

Raw links / artifacts (repeat for convenience):
- JIRA: OBS-4182 (redis eviction probe)
- JIRA: OBS-4190 (embedder shim + dashboard)
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/trace-probes/pull/212
- Slack: #observability thread 'trace-sampling-experiment'

End of notes.
